=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Package (SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-016)

**Preliminary note:** The Seller's "[STANDARD]", "FINAL" and "reviewer efficiency" labels don't bind Wattlebridge. The Disclosure Letter itself shows that several "[STANDARD]" items are live issues, so I've reviewed all 16 items. Legal points below should be confirmed by NSW counsel, and the DD-xxx source documents were not provided, so I've relied on the Disclosure Letter's summaries.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** A higher cap, opening at roughly 50% of price and falling back to around 30%. Specific indemnities sit outside the cap.
- **Recommendation:** Counter higher.
- **Reason:** AUD 4.8m is less than the combined disclosed exposures outside the cap, such as the Riverlark balance (AUD 3.2m) and the Bluefen revenue risk.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis, and a AUD 250k deductible basket (about 1% of price) with recovery only of the excess.
- **Buyer wants:** A lower de minimis, a "tipping" basket that recovers from the first dollar once breached, and a basket nearer 0.5% of price. Specific indemnities should be excluded from both.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the deductible structure.
- **Reason:** A deductible basket leaves the Buyer absorbing the first AUD 250k of losses, and the AUD 25k de minimis could exclude individual privacy or contract claims.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months for general claims, applied to all claims.
- **Buyer wants:** At least 24 months for general warranties, longer for tax, and the NSW contractual limitation period for fundamental warranties (see SPA-N-004).
- **Recommendation:** Reject the uniform application.
- **Reason:** 18 months may expire before the Buyer's first full post-completion audit, tax cycle or Bluefen/Ironquay issues crystallise.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (capacity, authority, title to shares) capped at 100% of price and time-limited to at least six years, subject to counsel confirming the NSW period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** Title defects are fundamental to what the Buyer is buying, and a 20% cap is inadequate for them.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Silent. The limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses (9.3, 12.8, 20.5) apply to "Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that nothing in the SPA limits liability for fraud, including fraud by the Seller's representatives. The non-reliance clause should not exclude fraudulent misrepresentation.
- **Recommendation:** Insist on an express carve-out.
- **Reason:** As drafted, the "any nature" wording could purport to cover fraud, and NSW law generally will not let a party contract out of liability for its own fraud, but the Buyer should not rely on that.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026) and public registers, "without limiting" specific disclosures (Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete 1.1 and 1.2. Disclosure only against specific warranties, with specific reference. The data room should not be deemed disclosed.
- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** The data room includes the very issues (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the export incident) that would otherwise support warranty claims, so general disclosure would hollow out the warranties.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (clause 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete. As a fallback, limit to the actual knowledge of named individuals, excluding constructive or discoverable knowledge, and make clear that specific indemnities are unaffected.
- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** The Buyer now knows about the Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and DD-006 issues, so this clause would remove recourse for the very risks the Buyer must price.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours to obtain consent. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- **Disclosure:** No final written consent. Conditions in clause 11.3 not evidenced. Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (about AUD 3.6m).
- **Buyer wants:** A hard condition precedent requiring a final written consent with all clause 11.3 conditions evidenced as satisfied, on terms acceptable to the Buyer. Include a longstop date and termination right. If the Buyer waives, require a price adjustment or specific indemnity for lost revenue.
- **Recommendation:** Make it a hard CP and delete the "treat as satisfied" wording.
- **Reason:** The Seller should not decide unilaterally that a condition is satisfied when it controls the outcome and the revenue at risk is material.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding, with a release "following Completion".
- **Disclosure:** Not repaid, and no final discharge of security included.
- **Buyer wants:** On a debt-free basis, repayment from the price at Completion, with an agreed-form payoff letter and discharge of all security (including PPSR registrations) delivered at Completion. The funds flow should show the payoff explicitly.
- **Recommendation:** Require payoff and discharge at Completion.
- **Reason:** A post-completion release leaves lender security over the business and shifts repayment risk to the Buyer, contrary to the debt-free basis.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** A matter for the Seller, not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Disclosure:** AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses. Payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:** Treat the bonuses and associated on-costs as debt-like items deducted from the price, with a specific indemnity covering any further employment costs triggered by Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Deduct from price, including on-costs (quantified with payroll advisers).
- **Reason:** On a cash-free, debt-free basis, these are Seller-generated liabilities and cannot be left to the Buyer.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate".
- **Disclosure:** Under DD-004 clause 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only once every SOW3 fee is paid. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open (not bank-verified). No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** A full indemnity for all Ironquay IP ownership and related claims, not limited to the SOW3 payment. Seller to pay the AUD 180,000 before Completion (or the amount is deducted). An executed confirmatory assignment as a CP.
- **Recommendation:** Expand the indemnity and make the assignment a CP.
- **Reason:** Until the fees are paid, the Company may not own the materials, so a payment-only indemnity does not protect ownership.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter" not expected to be material.
- **Disclosure:** Download link sent to an unintended external address. Up to about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Access, scope and notification obligations are unknown.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific indemnity covering regulatory, notification, remediation, and third-party losses, outside the basket and de minimis and with a separate or uncapped limit. Pre-completion forensic investigation with Buyer participation. Seller to bear response costs.
- **Recommendation:** Specific indemnity and a privacy assessment before signing.
- **Reason:** The disclosure itself says access, scope and notification status are undetermined, so the Seller's materiality view is unsupported. Privacy counsel should confirm whether the Privacy Act's eligible data breach scheme applies.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals (AUD 110k each, AUD 330k total) described as ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Disclosure:** Not stated whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Read together for timing and scope.
- **Buyer wants:** The contracts produced, the timing and scope confirmed, and any pre-completion or non-ordinary-course element treated as a debt-like item. A warranty that no contracts have been split to avoid approval thresholds.
- **Recommendation:** Require contracts and classify before agreeing the price.
- **Reason:** The "ordinary course" label is unverified, and the aggregate is material.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** A single general regime for all claims.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate categories with different caps and time limits: general warranties; fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority); tax; specific indemnities (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the export incident, bonuses, Sandbar as needed); and fraud (unlimited).
- **Recommendation:** Adopt separate categories.
- **Reason:** A single regime subjects identified specific risks to the general cap and basket, which the Buyer could not reasonably have priced.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Share register at DD-012 shows Harbourglass as holder of 100% of shares.
- **Disclosure:** Does not state that the Buyer has verified title.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification before signing: current and historical ASIC extracts, inspection of the original register, the share certificates and transfer forms, a PPSR search over the shares, and confirmation of stamp duty treatment. A title warranty backed by the fundamental regime.
- **Recommendation:** Complete verification pre-signing.
- **Reason:** The Seller's register is the only source, and the Buyer has not checked it.

### SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Dedicated tax warranties and a pre-completion tax indemnity, with a time limit running to the statute of limitations plus a buffer. IP ownership warranties (including contributor assignments and open-source use) outside the general cap and basket.
- **Recommendation:** Separate tax indemnity and IP warranties.
- **Reason:** The Disclosure Letter contains no tax disclosure, so tax exposure is unpriced, and IP ownership is central to a SaaS acquisition.

---

### Other items to check (not in the 16)
- **DD-009 (Mossvale):** Confirm whether the assignment restriction is triggered by a share sale. If so, obtain consent as a CP.
- **DD-007 (office lease):** Confirm whether landlord consent is needed for the share sale, since the disclosure only refers to a notification obligation.
- **Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6:** Treat the "not material" label on the export incident with caution (see SPA-N-012).

### Priority actions
1. Reject the FINAL and "no further scrutiny" framing and table a full mark-up.
2. Make Bluefen, Riverlark payoff and Ironquay assignment conditions precedent.
3. Delete general data room disclosure (SPA-N-006) and the buyer-knowledge qualifier (SPA-N-007).
4. Add specific indemnities for Ironquay, the export incident, bonuses, and tax.
5. Adjust the funds flow for debt-like items (Riverlark, bonuses and on-costs, Ironquay's AUD 180k).
6. Complete independent title verification before signing.
7. Engage privacy counsel on the export incident and NSW counsel on limitation periods and fraud carve-out wording.
